title: Procurement ≠ Purchasing
purpose: Distinguish the transaction of buying from the broader professional lifecycle without devaluing operational purchasing.

cases.need: Replacement safety gloves from approved catalog supplier
cases.context: Standard specification, contracted price, approved supplier, stock route known.

cases.need: New vibration-monitoring service for three European plants
cases.context: Business requirement still vague; multiple supplier models; data access and service levels matter; no current contract.

core_distinction.purchasing: The operational act/process of ordering goods or services through an established path.
core_distinction.procurement: The broader discipline of understanding need, shaping the buying path, sourcing/assessing suppliers, commercial decision-making, contracting, supplier/risk management and lifecycle value — which may include purchasing.

traps: Procurement begins only when an RFQ is launched.
A purchase order is the entire Procurement lifecycle.
strong_principle: Use the amount of Procurement work the need actually requires. Routine purchasing can be correct professional work; complex/novel needs require broader investigation and commercial judgment.
